Theme

Latin word

ut

conjunction, with the indicative; often answered by ita or sīc · Wiktionary

as; granted that, even supposing; as, for instance (before the example); how (of health and state); like, as; in order to, so that (not); for, considering, relative to (the times, the person); so that, in order to; so that … not; so … that; that (it happens that; I ask that); when, as soon as

In this lexicon

  • as

    the recommended word · classical · Sen. Ep. 4.1: persevērā ut coepistī; Ter. And. 310: Age age, ut libet.; Traupman 273

  • even if

    also used · classical · Ov. Pont. 3.4.79: ut dēsint vīrēs, tamen est laudanda voluntās (Lewis & Short)

  • example

    also used · classical · Traupman 221: genus masculīnum, ut “hic magister”

  • how

    also used · classical · Plaut. Trin. 48–49: ut valēs, Megarōnidēs?; Traupman 330

  • like

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Sen. 44: hominēs capiantur ut piscēs

  • purpose

    also used · classical · Cic. Off. 3.42: ēnītī et contendere dēbet quam maximē possit, ut vincat; Caes. BG 1.48: eō cōnsiliō utī frūmentō commeātūque … Caesarem interclūderet

  • relatively

    also used · classical · Cic. Brut. 102: scrīptor, ut temporibus illīs, lūculentus (Lewis & Short); Cic. Sen. 12: multae, ut in homine Rōmānō, litterae (Lewis & Short); Cic. Fam. 12.2.2: nōnnihil, ut in tantīs malīs, est prōfectum (Lewis & Short)

  • so that

    the recommended word · classical · Ov. Ars 2.107: ut amēris, amābilis estō; Quint. 6.1.46: date puerō pānem, nē plōret

  • so … that

    the recommended word · classical · Sen. Ep. 57.1: tantum lutī tōtā viā fuit ut possim vidērī nihilōminus nāvigāsse; Liv. 21.56.7: ita torpentēs gelū in castra rediēre ut vix laetitiam victōriae sentīrent

  • that

    also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.101: ita fit, ut ratiō praesit, appetītus obtemperet

  • when

    also used · classical · Cic. Att. 5.1.3: ut vēnī in Arpīnās; Traupman 406
